codex:
1. **Verdict: IMPROVE.** A materially stronger, immediately provable whole-paper statement is already latent in `def:benchmarks` and `thm:all-regime-bracket`: with \(\ell_d=\log(ed)\),
\[
U_{n,d}=\min(1,d/n)\le \ell_d\,L_{n,d},
\]
because \(\ell_d\min\{1,d/(n\ell_d)\}\ge \min\{1,d/n\}\). Hence the existing proofs give
\[
c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon\log(ed)\,L_{n,d}
\]
uniformly in \(n,d\). The note is therefore an all-regime logarithmic minimax characterization, not merely an unspecified bracket. It also contains an unreported lower-bound phase diagram: for \(n>1\),
\[
L_{n,d}=
\begin{cases}
d/n, & d\le n^{1/3},\\
n^{-2/3}, & n^{1/3}<d\le n^{1/3}\log(ed),\\
d/[n\log(ed)], & n^{1/3}\log(ed)<d<n\log(ed),\\
1, & d\ge n\log(ed),
\end{cases}
\]
with the boundary equalities interpreted harmlessly. Thus the note has a real plateau-to-unknown-mass elbow at \(d\asymp n^{1/3}\log(ed)\), in addition to the dense elbow \(d=n^{1/3}\) and impossibility saturation \(d\asymp n\log(ed)\). No inspected source or present proof establishes the exact \(\rho(n,d)\), so `oeq:sharp-all-regime-frontier` must remain OPEN.

2. **Concrete scoped directive.** Strengthen `thm:all-regime-bracket` (or add `prop:log-sharp-all-regime-frontier` depending only on `def:benchmarks` and `thm:all-regime-bracket`) with the displayed \(C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d}\) upper bound and its three-line proof. Add `prop:lower-benchmark-phase-diagram` spelling out the four branches above and explicitly relating the first branch to `thm:dense-frontier`. Keep `oeq:sharp-all-regime-frontier` unchanged except to say that it asks to remove the remaining at-most-\(\log(ed)\) factor and determine which displayed elbow(s) are genuine. Do not promote `def:grouped-reconstruction-handle` to an estimator result: it currently gives no explicit split, shells, \(K\), grid, factorial statistic, covariance bound, feasibility tolerance, or risk proof. Either rename its defined object “candidate grouped-reconstruction blueprint” or supply those objects and prove a new `thm:grouped-reconstruction-upper`, followed by a same-class `thm:matching-frontier-lower`, before claiming it as a construction. Synchronize `tldr`, `project_justification.fill`, `technical_internal_limitation`, and `honest_scope`. The TL;DR should say “difference of two armwise ratios,” foreground “all-regime logarithmic characterization,” and reserve “exact frontier” for the open question. `project_justification.fill` should replace “concrete positive grouped-moment handle” with “an explicit open blueprint for a positive grouped-moment construction” unless the missing estimator theorem is supplied. These changes directly resolve both `PROSE-OPEN-OVERCLAIM` warnings: the TL;DR warning is mainly a lexical false positive, since it already calls the exact rate open, but the Fill warning is substantively justified because a checklist-style definition is not a constructed or risk-controlled estimator.

3. **Novelty/tier verdict.** Field-tier positioning survives the exact question being open, but only after the paper is framed as the first same-class, all-regime, logarithmically sharp squared-\(W_1\) characterization plus an exact \(d/n\) dense frontier and exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary. Selling it as an exact sparse-to-dense frontier would not survive review. The proved identification and empirical upper bound alone are elementary, and the dense result resembles the \(n\asymp d^3\) elbow in unlabeled-distribution work; the tier-relevant contribution is the combination of the same-class law-valued lower mechanisms with the global logarithmic approximation and its explicit phase diagram. A future exact-rate paper still requires the fully tuned `def:grouped-reconstruction-handle` construction and a matching unrestricted-class converse.

4. **Soundness/laundering check.** The closest causal anchor class is, at the observed-experiment level, the same class: Zeng–Balakrishnan–Han–Kennedy allow arbitrary categorical masses including zeros, binary treatment/outcome, unknown propensities bounded by \(\epsilon\), and unrestricted arm regressions. `lem:observed-law-identification` shows that the note’s potential-outcome formulation maps onto exactly those observed tables, so the main upper and minimax statements are not quietly restricted relative to that anchor. The anchor’s target is scalar, however, so none of its rates can be restated as a CATE-law rate. Vinayak–Kong–Kakade is not the same class: it has \(N\) iid latent parameter pairs, equal entity weighting, and a common fixed \(t\) trials in each arm. Han–Jiao–Weissman has one multinomial probability per label and estimates the sorted probability vector; Lee–Baćak–Kennedy conditions on observed heterogeneous trial counts and assumes smooth mixing densities. Those papers are analogies, not theorem donors for the headline. The converse transfer in `thm:scalar-transfer-lower` is nevertheless legitimate upward transfer: its displayed four-cell table is a genuine \(e_x=1/2\) subfamily of \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), \(\int|t|\,dG_P=\frac12\|r-s\|_1\), and the donor-to-causal observation kernel has the correct information direction. Likewise, `thm:separated-atom-lower` uses only a valid subclass while the supremum remains over the full class. The only laundering risk is rhetorical treatment of `def:grouped-reconstruction-handle` as a delivered construction.

5. **Evidence from note and anchor hypotheses.** Zeng et al., pp. 4 and 9–10, define \(n\) iid \((X,A,Y)\), \(X\in[d]\), binary \(A,Y\), arbitrary \(p_k\), \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\), unrestricted \(\mu_{ak}\), and in Theorem 2 study only the scalar regression mean/ATE lower bound. Vinayak et al., pp. 3–7 and Theorems 2.1–2.2, observe \(N\) iid latent pairs \((p_i,q_i)\) through exactly \(t\) binomial trials per coordinate and target the equally weighted change mixing law. Han et al., pp. 1–7 and Theorem 1, start from one discrete probability vector \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_S)\), estimate its sorted version, and use the uniform measure on the multiset \(\{p_i\}\); there are no treated-control ratios or endogenous target masses. Lee et al., Sections 2.1 and 3/Corollary 2, require Hölder-smooth mixing densities and observed trial counts and prove pointwise KDE/density-difference bounds, not unrestricted atomic \(W_1\)-law recovery. These hypotheses support the note’s non-subsumption claim, while also requiring the sharper wording that Zeng supplies the same observed model class but a different scalar target.
